content.title: Collect SMS Opt-In Consent
content.summary: Carriers require explicit, checkbox-based consent before you can text anyone. Get it right the first time to speed up approval and avoid blocked messages.

sections.heading: Why Proper Consent Matters
sections.body: A phone number alone is not consent, and neither is someone simply submitting a form. To send SMS, carriers require an explicit, unchecked consent checkbox that names your business and describes what messages the person will receive. Getting this right the first time is the single biggest thing you can do to speed up approval and avoid rejections.

rows.label: Phone number field
rows.value: Clearly labeled and optional to fill in

rows.label: Unchecked checkbox
rows.value: Person actively checks it; never pre-checked

rows.label: Message description
rows.value: What texts they will receive (reminders, offers, etc.)

rows.label: Standard disclosures
rows.value: Msg & data rates, frequency, STOP and HELP

rows.label: Terms & Privacy
rows.value: Separate checkbox with links to both policies

sections.heading: Split Consent by Message Type
sections.body: If you send both transactional messages (reminders, account notices) and marketing messages (promotions, offers), each type needs its own checkbox. Add a third checkbox for Terms of Service and Privacy Policy acceptance with links. Combining them into one box is the number one reason forms get rejected.
bullets: Transactional: appointment and account texts with disclosures
Marketing: offers and promotions, plus "consent is not required"
Terms & Privacy: separate acknowledgement with links

sidebar.heading: At a glance

facts.label: Privacy Policy
facts.value: Must state data is not sold

sidebar.callout_text: A single checkbox covering all SMS types, or wording like "by submitting this form you agree to receive texts," will fail carrier review. Keep message types on separate boxes.

sections.heading: Privacy Policy That Passes Review
sections.body: Your Privacy Policy must state plainly that you do not sell or share opt-in data. Without this, your registration can be rejected. Include this language:
bullets: "We do not sell or share mobile numbers or SMS consent"
Data shared only with service providers to operate SMS
Include frequency, rates, STOP and HELP disclosures

sections.heading: Write Compliant Sample Messages
sections.body: When you register, your sample messages must include your brand name and STOP/HELP language. Generic placeholders get rejected.

sections.heading: What Gets a Form Rejected
sections.body: Avoid these common mistakes to clear review on the first attempt.
bullets: One combined checkbox covering all SMS types
Consent implied just by submitting the form
Missing STOP, HELP, or frequency disclosures

sections.heading: Pre-Submission Checklist
bullets: Business name matches registration, website, and samples
Dedicated, optional phone number field present
Separate unchecked checkboxes for each message type
Terms and Privacy links present with own checkbox
Sample messages include brand name and real content

sidebar.heading: Required disclosures
sidebar.callout_text: Your Salesmsg team is happy to review your opt-in form before you submit. A two-minute check now can save days of back-and-forth with the carriers.

cta.text: Our team will check your opt-in form before you submit to carriers.
